plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is a mainstay of winter gardens, with thousands of cultivars in many flower forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak in midwinter in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant that produces all true tea, and Camellia japonica seed oil has long been used in Japan for hair care and cooking.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that blooms on bare branches in the cold, producing fragrant five-petaled flowers. It is a beloved symbol of perseverance and the coming of spring in East Asian culture.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated across China, Japan, Korea, and Vietnam, and in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms appear weeks before cherry blossoms, and the fruits are pickled into umeboshi or made into plum wine.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pink. It tolerates frost and snow and brings color to the winter woodland garden.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; grown in shaded gardens across temperate regions
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant are toxic, and the flowers can bloom through snow because the plant produces tiny amounts of heat in its tissues.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A large shrub bearing the biggest flower head in the protea family, with a showy crown of pink-tipped bracts around a central cluster of true flowers. It is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and fire-prone habitats.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere late spring to summer, with flowers present through January in cultivation
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa; cultivated in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its flower heads can reach 30 cm across.
